name: Setlocenia

attributes.attribute: her name carries the sense of goddess of long life
compared conceptually, not etymologically, with the Irish Buanann

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Setlocenia is a minor goddess of early northern Britain. Her name carries the sense of goddess of long life or the long-lived one. Her worship rests on a single record, an invocation at Maryport in Cumberland. No fuller story of her survives. The one inscription shows a deity of prosperity and long life. She likely guarded a long and healthy existence along with the goods that go with it. Writers compare her in concept, though not in word origin, with the Irish Buanann.

okr.objective: Document Setlocenia, the long-life goddess known from one British inscription.
key_results: Record the sense of her name as goddess of long life
Locate her single invocation at Maryport in Cumberland
Record the conceptual comparison with the Irish Buanann
